title: Email: 16 Mar Planned Outages, Go/No-Go by 06:30

fields.subject: 16 Mar planned outages — go/no-go by 06:30
fields.body:
Good morning,

We have six 345 kV outages on the board for today, and I need a go/no-go on each one.

The big one is the Hartley AT-1 replacement: a 14-hour outage. The crew of 9 is already on site, and the 120-ton crane is booked at $18,000 a day. The contractor wants our answer by 06:30. After that they start billing standby.

The other five are line maintenance on 345 kV circuits out of Iron Range, Cloquet and North Shore. The crews are due to report between 07:00 and 08:00. Switching orders are in the attached board.

Separately, the timing team's vendor has a firmware push to the GPS clocks at four substations scheduled for 10:00. The clocks have to be restarted for it to take effect.

Do any of these still go ahead? I'm at the planning desk and can call the crews and the contractor as soon as I have your decision.

Thanks,
fields.signature:
Outage Coordinator
Day Planning Desk | Northern Lakes Transmission Operations
Duluth, MN

instructorNote: Before you hand this over, tell the room it is now 06:00 and that day supervisor Walter Nakamura has taken over from the night shift. This is a pressure inject that pits money and crew time against the G3 watch and the 11:00–17:00 CDT arrival window. Watch for the TOM to defer all six 345 kV outages, including Hartley AT-1, and log why (NGDOP 4, Condition 1 review, then the Condition 2 deferral). Watch for TIME to postpone the clock firmware push and confirm that the holdover clocks and the fiber backup time source are healthy (NGDOP 7). Watch for the CRSS to brief Walter Nakamura on the condition and the log.

citations.quote: | Condition | Predetermined trigger | Actions | |---|---|---| | **Condition 1: Watch** | SWPC Geomagnetic Storm Watch for G3 or higher, or a CME discussion with an arrival window in the next 36 hours,

Substation clocks and phasor measurement units use GPS time. A geomagnetic storm of G4 or higher can degrade GNSS. NLTO has holdover clocks at 14 substations with 24 hours of holdover and a backup net
